title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 18. The Play on Lake Narendra
html:
The Lord meets the devotees of Gauda and Himself bows to the Vaishnavas; the festival Deities come to Lake Narendra, and Gaura plays in the water with His devotees, as Krishna once did with the gopis in the Yamuna; then the Lord goes to the temple and beholds Jagannatha

Verse 1

भावमासाद्य ते सर्वे परमानन्दविह्वलाः।
नमन्ति दण्डवद्भूमौ हरिध्वनिसमन्विताः॥१॥

bhāvamāsādya te sarve paramānandavihvalāḥ|
namanti daṇḍavadbhūmau haridhvanisamanvitāḥ||1||

bhavam — ecstatic feeling; asadya — attaining; te — they; sarve — all; parama-ananda-vihvalah — overwhelmed by supreme bliss; namanti — bow; danda-vat — like a rod; bhumau — on the ground; hari-dhvani-samanvitah — with cries of "Hari!".

1Seized by ecstatic feeling, overwhelmed by supreme bliss, they all fall flat on the ground like rods, crying "Hari!"

Verse 2

ईश्वरोऽपि नमश्चक्रे वैष्णवैः सह वैष्णवान्।
दर्शयन्नाश्रमादीनां वैष्णवाराधने विधिम्॥२॥

īśvaro'pi namaścakre vaiṣṇavaiḥ saha vaiṣṇavān|
darśayannāśramādīnāṁ vaiṣṇavārādhane vidhim||2||

ishvarah — the Lord; api — too; namah chakre — bowed; vaishnavaih saha — together with the Vaishnavas; vaishnavan — to the Vaishnavas; darshayan — showing; ashrama-adinam — for (those of every) ashrama and the rest; vaishnava-aradhane — in the worship of Vaishnavas; vidhim — the rule.

2And the Lord too, together with the Vaishnavas, bowed to the Vaishnavas, showing people of every ashrama and station how the Vaishnavas are to be honoured.

Verse 3

अपि चेत् सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक्।
साधुरेव स मन्तव्य इति कृष्णमुखोदितम्॥३॥

api cet sudurācāro bhajate māmananyabhāk|
sādhureva sa mantavya iti kṛṣṇamukhoditam||3||

api chet — even if; su-durachara — one of very bad conduct; bhajate — worships; mam — Me; ananya-bhak — devoted to no other; sadhuh — a saint; eva — certainly; sah — he; mantavyah — is to be considered; iti — thus; krishna-mukha-uditam — spoken by the mouth of Krishna.

3"Even if a man's conduct has been very bad, if he worships Me with devotion to no other, he must certainly be regarded as a saint"1 — so it was spoken by the mouth of Krishna.

Verse 4

प्रकाश्य जनसंघानां हिताय जगदीश्वरः।
वैष्णवान् वन्दनं चक्रे न्यासादिमदखण्डनम्॥४॥

prakāśya janasaṁghānāṁ hitāya jagadīśvaraḥ|
vaiṣṇavān vandanaṁ cakre nyāsādimadakhaṇḍanam||4||

prakashya — revealing (this); jana-sanghanam — of the multitudes; hitaya — for the good; jagat-ishvarah — the Lord of the world; vaishnavan — to the Vaishnavas; vandanam chakre — offered homage; nyasa-adi-mada-khandanam — which shatters the pride of sannyasa and the like.

4Having revealed this for the good of all people, the Lord of the world paid homage to the Vaishnavas — a homage that shatters the pride of sannyasa and every other pride.

Verse 5

कम्पाश्रुपुलकव्याप्ता धूलिमण्डितविग्रहाः।
नृत्यन्तश्च नमन्तश्च गायन्तस्ते पुनः पुनः॥५॥

kampāśrupulakavyāptā dhūlimaṇḍitavigrahāḥ|
nṛtyantaśca namantaśca gāyantaste punaḥ punaḥ||5||

kampa-ashru-pulaka-vyaptah — pervaded by trembling, tears and bristling hair; dhuli-mandita-vigrahah — their bodies adorned with dust; nrityantah — dancing; cha — and; namantah — bowing; cha — and; gayantah — singing; te — they; punah punah — again and again.

5Pervaded by trembling, tears and bristling hair, their bodies adorned with dust, they danced, bowed and sang again and again.

Verse 6

गौराङ्गदर्शनानन्दमत्ताः स्वं न विदन्ति ते।
गौराङ्गो जय गौराङ्ग गौराङ्ग इति वादिनः॥६॥

gaurāṅgadarśanānandamattāḥ svaṁ na vidanti te|
gaurāṅgo jaya gaurāṅga gaurāṅga iti vādinaḥ||6||

gauranga-darshana-ananda-mattah — intoxicated with the bliss of seeing Gauranga; svam — themselves; na — not; vidanti — know; te — they; gaurangah — "Gauranga!"; jaya — glory; gauranga — O Gauranga; gauranga — Gauranga; iti — thus; vadinah — crying.

6Intoxicated with the bliss of seeing Gauranga, they forgot themselves and only cried, "Gauranga! Glory to Gauranga! Gauranga!"

Verse 7

तथा वैष्णवपत्न्यश्च दूरे दृष्ट्वा महाप्रभुम्।
तासां प्रेमपराकाष्ठां को वेद कोऽपि संवदेत्॥७॥

tathā vaiṣṇavapatnyaśca dūre dṛṣṭvā mahāprabhum|
tāsāṁ premaparākāṣṭhāṁ ko veda ko'pi saṁvadet||7||

tatha — likewise; vaishnava-patnyah — the wives of the Vaishnavas; cha — and; dure — from afar; drishtva — seeing; maha-prabhum — Mahaprabhu; tasam — their; prema-para-kashtham — summit of love; kah — who; veda — knows; kah api — who at all; samvadet — could describe.

7So too did the wives of the Vaishnavas, who saw Mahaprabhu from afar — but who knows the summit of their love, who could ever describe it?

Verse 8

ततस्ताः श्रीहरेर्भक्तिसंव्यापिन्यो न संशयः।
श्रीकृष्णनामपूर्णास्याः प्रेमाश्रुपुलकान्विताः॥८॥

tatastāḥ śrīharerbhaktisaṁvyāpinyo na saṁśayaḥ|
śrīkṛṣṇanāmapūrṇāsyāḥ premāśrupulakānvitāḥ||8||

tatah — therefore; tah — they; shri-hareh — for Sri Hari; bhakti-samvyapinyah — pervaded by devotion; na samshayah — there is no doubt; shri-krishna-nama-purna-asyah — their mouths full of Sri Krishna's name; prema-ashru-pulaka-anvitah — with tears of love and bristling hair.

8Truly they were filled with devotion to Sri Hari, of that there is no doubt: their mouths were full of Sri Krishna's name, and they were bathed in tears of love, their hair standing on end.

Verse 9

तदैव रामकृष्णौ श्रीयात्रागोविन्द एव च।
जलक्रीडार्थमायातौ नरेन्द्रसरसि ध्रुवम्॥९॥

tadaiva rāmakṛṣṇau śrīyātrāgovinda eva ca|
jalakrīḍārthamāyātau narendrasarasi dhruvam||9||

tada eva — just then; rama-krishnau — Rama and Krishna; shri-yatra-govindah — Sri Yatra-Govinda; eva cha — and also; jala-krida-artham — for water-play; ayatau — came; narendra-sarasi — to Lake Narendra; dhruvam — indeed.

9Just then Rama and Krishna, and Sri Yatra-Govinda too2, came to Lake Narendra for play in the water.

Verse 10

महाविभूतिसंयुक्ता हरिसंकीर्तनादिभिः।
मण्डिता भक्तवर्गैश्च गौरगोविन्दकिङ्कराः॥१०॥

mahāvibhūtisaṁyuktā harisaṁkīrtanādibhiḥ|
maṇḍitā bhaktavargaiśca gauragovindakiṅkarāḥ||10||

maha-vibhuti-samyuktah — with great pomp; hari-sankirtana-adibhih — with the sankirtana of Hari and the rest; manditah — adorned; bhakta-vargaih — with throngs of devotees; cha — and; gaura-govinda-kinkarah — the servants of Gaura and of Govinda.

10There too were the servants of Gaura and of Govinda — with great pomp, adorned with the sankirtana of Hari's name, with throngs of devotees and all the rest.

Verse 11

नावमासाद्य तावच्च विहरन्तो महामुदः।
गोविन्दरामकृष्णाश्च कुर्वन्ति जलकौतुकम्॥११॥

nāvamāsādya tāvacca viharanto mahāmudaḥ|
govindarāmakṛṣṇāśca kurvanti jalakautukam||11||

navam — a boat; asadya — boarding; tavat — then; cha — and; viharantah — sporting; maha-mudah — in great joy; govinda-rama-krishnah — Govinda, Rama and Krishna; cha — and; kurvanti — make; jala-kautukam — merry play on the water.

11And Govinda, Rama and Krishna, boarding a boat, make merry upon the water in great joy.

Verse 12

सभक्तो गौरचन्द्रश्च जलमाविश्य कौतुकी।
गदाधररसोल्लासी नित्यानन्दसुखप्रदः॥१२॥

sabhakto gauracandraśca jalamāviśya kautukī|
gadādhararasollāsī nityānandasukhapradaḥ||12||

sa-bhaktah — with His devotees; gaurachandrah — Gaurachandra; cha — and; jalam — the water; avishya — entering; kautuki — playful; gadadhara-rasa-ullasi — delighting in rasa with Gadadhara; nityananda-sukha-pradah — giving joy to Nityananda.

12Gaurachandra too entered the water with His devotees, playfully — He who delights in rasa with Gadadhara and gives joy to Nityananda.

Verse 13

अद्वैताचार्यप्रेष्ठश्च स्वरूपाद्यैः समन्वितः।
क्रीडति परमानन्दं यमुनायां यथा पुरा॥१३॥

advaitācāryapreṣṭhaśca svarūpādyaiḥ samanvitaḥ|
krīḍati paramānandaṁ yamunāyāṁ yathā purā||13||

advaita-acharya-preshthah — the dearest of Advaita Acharya; cha — and; svarupa-adyaih — by Svarupa and the others; samanvitah — accompanied; kridati — sports; parama-anandam — in supreme bliss; yamunayam — in the Yamuna; yatha — as; pura — of old.

13The dearest of Advaita Acharya, with Svarupa and the others, sports in supreme bliss, as of old in the Yamuna.

Verse 14

स सनातनरूपश्रीरघुनाथेश्वरो हरिः।
मुरारिरामश्रीवासगौरीदासप्रियोऽपि यः॥१४॥

sa sanātanarūpaśrīraghunātheśvaro hariḥ|
murārirāmaśrīvāsagaurīdāsapriyo'pi yaḥ||14||

sah — that; sanatana-rupa-shri-raghunatha-ishvarah — Lord of Sanatana, Rupa and Sri Raghunatha; harih — Hari; murari-rama-shrivasa-gauridasa-priyah — dear to Murari, Rama, Srivasa and Gauridasa; api — also; yah — who.

14That Hari, the Lord of Sanatana, Rupa and Sri Raghunatha, dear to Murari, Rama, Srivasa and Gauridasa,

Verse 15

परमानन्दपुरीवंशीरामानन्दसहायवान्।
काशीश्वरमानदाता हरिदासप्रियंकरः॥१५॥

paramānandapurīvaṁśīrāmānandasahāyavān|
kāśīśvaramānadātā haridāsapriyaṁkaraḥ||15||

paramananda-puri-vamshi-ramananda-sahayavan — having as His helpers Paramananda Puri, Vamshi and Ramananda; kashishvara-mana-data — giver of honour to Kashishvara; haridasa-priyamkarah — who delights Haridasa.

15who has as His helpers Paramananda Puri, Vamshi3 and Ramananda, who gives honour to Kashishvara and delight to Haridasa —

Verse 16

स्वप्रकाशतया सर्वभक्तैश्च विपिनेश्वरः।
सहैव क्रीडति गौरगोविन्दः शचीनन्दनः॥१६॥

svaprakāśatayā sarvabhaktaiśca vipineśvaraḥ|
sahaiva krīḍati gauragovindaḥ śacīnandanaḥ||16||

sva-prakashataya — by His self-manifestation (prakasha); sarva-bhaktaih — with all the devotees; cha — and; vipina-ishvarah — the Lord of the (Vrindavana) forests; saha eva — together with each; kridati — sports; gaura-govindah — Gaura-Govinda; shachi-nandanah — the son of Shachi.

16Gaura-Govinda, the Lord of the Vrindavana forests, the son of Shachi, manifesting Himself many times over4, sports together with each of His devotees.

Verse 17

सर्वे जानन्ति क्रीडति गौराङ्गो हि मया समम्।
तेन सार्धं भक्तगणाः कुर्वन्ति जलकौतुकम्॥१७॥

sarve jānanti krīḍati gaurāṅgo hi mayā samam|
tena sārdhaṁ bhaktagaṇāḥ kurvanti jalakautukam||17||

sarve — all; jananti — think; kridati — sports; gaurangah — Gauranga; hi — indeed; maya samam — with me; tena sardham — together with Him; bhakta-ganah — the devotees; kurvanti — make; jala-kautukam — merry play on the water.

17Each one thinks, "It is with me that Gauranga is playing," and so the devotees make merry in the water together with Him.

Verse 18

गोपीभिः सह गोविन्दो यमुनायां यथा पुरा।
अकरोद्विविधां क्रीडां श्रीरासरसकौतुकी॥१८॥

gopībhiḥ saha govindo yamunāyāṁ yathā purā|
akarodvividhāṁ krīḍāṁ śrīrāsarasakautukī||18||

gopibhih saha — with the gopis; govindah — Govinda; yamunayam — in the Yamuna; yatha — as; pura — once; akarot — performed; vividham — various; kridam — play; shri-rasa-rasa-kautuki — eager for the rasa of the rasa dance.

18So once in the Yamuna Govinda, eager for the rasa of the rasa dance, played many kinds of games with the gopis,

Verse 19

यथा गोपीजनाः कृष्णं जलक्रीडापरायणम्।
सुखयन्ति निजप्रेमविलासनवविभ्रमैः॥१९॥

yathā gopījanāḥ kṛṣṇaṁ jalakrīḍāparāyaṇam|
sukhayanti nijapremavilāsanavavibhramaiḥ||19||

yatha — as; gopi-janah — the gopis; krishnam — Krishna; jala-krida-parayanam — absorbed in water-play; sukhayanti — delight; nija-prema-vilasa-nava-vibhramaih — with ever-new graceful plays of their love.

19and the gopis delighted Krishna, absorbed in water-play, with the ever-new graceful plays of their love.

Verse 20

एवं जलविहारं च कारयित्वा यथोचितम्।
गौराङ्गो रामकृष्णौ श्रीयात्रागोविन्द एव च॥२०॥

evaṁ jalavihāraṁ ca kārayitvā yathocitam|
gaurāṅgo rāmakṛṣṇau śrīyātrāgovinda eva ca||20||

evam — thus; jala-viharam — water-play; cha — and; karayitva — having held; yatha-uchitam — as befitted; gaurangah — Gauranga; rama-krishnau — Rama and Krishna; shri-yatra-govindah — Sri Yatra-Govinda; eva cha — and also.

20Having thus held the water-play as befitted, Gauranga, and Rama and Krishna, and Sri Yatra-Govinda

Verse 21

उत्तिष्ठन्ति जलह्रदाद्भूषिता भूषणोत्तमैः।
पूजिताश्चोपहारैश्च स्वस्वभृत्यसमन्विताः॥२१॥

uttiṣṭhanti jalahradādbhūṣitā bhūṣaṇottamaiḥ|
pūjitāścopahāraiśca svasvabhṛtyasamanvitāḥ||21||

uttishthanti — rise; jala-hradat — from the lake; bhushitah — adorned; bhushana-uttamaih — with the finest ornaments; pujitah — worshipped; cha — and; upaharaih — with offerings; cha — and; sva-sva-bhritya-samanvitah — each with his own servants.

21rise from the lake; They are adorned with the finest ornaments and worshipped with offerings, and each is attended by His own servants.

Verse 22

नृत्यवाद्यसुगानाद्यैर्मन्दिरं प्रययुः सुखम्।
रामकृष्णौ च श्रीयात्रागोविन्दः स्वजनैः सह॥२२॥

nṛtyavādyasugānādyairmandiraṁ prayayuḥ sukham|
rāmakṛṣṇau ca śrīyātrāgovindaḥ svajanaiḥ saha||22||

nritya-vadya-su-gana-adyaih — with dancing, music, sweet singing and the rest; mandiram — to the temple; prayayuh — went; sukham — joyfully; rama-krishnau — Rama and Krishna; cha — and; shri-yatra-govindah — Sri Yatra-Govinda; sva-janaih saha — with their own people.

22With dancing, music, sweet singing and the rest, Rama and Krishna and Sri Yatra-Govinda joyfully went with Their own people to the temple.

Verse 23

गौराङ्गश्च निजैर्भक्तैः कृष्णसंकीर्तनैः परैः।
समं भक्तावेशतया ययौ श्रीहरिमन्दिरम्॥२३॥

gaurāṅgaśca nijairbhaktaiḥ kṛṣṇasaṁkīrtanaiḥ paraiḥ|
samaṁ bhaktāveśatayā yayau śrīharimandiram||23||

gaurangah — Gauranga; cha — and; nijaih — with His own; bhaktaih — devotees; krishna-sankirtanaih — with the sankirtana of Krishna; paraih — supreme; samam — together; bhakta-aveshataya — absorbed in the mood of a devotee; yayau — went; shri-hari-mandiram — to the temple of Sri Hari.

23And Gauranga, with His own devotees and with the supreme sankirtana of Krishna, went in the mood of a devotee to the temple of Sri Hari.

Verse 24

जगन्नाथमुखं दृष्ट्वा सभक्तः प्रेमविह्वलः।
गरुडस्तम्भमाश्रित्य स्थितो दर्शनलालसः॥२४॥

jagannāthamukhaṁ dṛṣṭvā sabhaktaḥ premavihvalaḥ|
garuḍastambhamāśritya sthito darśanalālasaḥ||24||

jagannatha-mukham — the face of Jagannatha; drishtva — seeing; sa-bhaktah — with the devotees; prema-vihvalah — overwhelmed with love; garuda-stambham — the Garuda pillar; ashritya — leaning against; sthitah — stood; darshana-lalasah — longing for the sight.

24Seeing the face of Jagannatha, He and His devotees were overwhelmed with love, and leaning against the Garuda pillar He stood, longing to behold Him.

Verse 25

नित्यानन्दसुखोल्लासी भक्तवर्गसमन्वितः।
द्वौ पार्श्वे पश्यति गौरचन्द्रो रामजनार्दनौ॥२५॥

nityānandasukhollāsī bhaktavargasamanvitaḥ|
dvau pārśve paśyati gauracandro rāmajanārdanau||25||

nityananda-sukha-ullasi — rejoicing in Nityananda's joy; bhakta-varga-samanvitah — surrounded by His devotees; dvau — the two; parshve — at either side; pashyati — sees; gaurachandrah — Gaurachandra; rama-janardanau — Rama and Janardana.

25Rejoicing in Nityananda's joy, surrounded by His devotees, Gaurachandra sees the two side by side — Rama and Janardana5.

Thus ends the eighteenth sarga, "The Play on Lake Narendra" (Narendra-saro-vihara), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Bhagavad-gita 9.30.
  2. Rama, Krishna and Yatra-Govinda are festival Deities (utsava-murtis) of the Jagannatha temple, who at the Chandana-yatra festival are brought to Lake Narendra for play in a boat.
  3. Vamshi: probably Vamshivadana, a companion of the Lord.
  4. Literally, "by His self-manifestation": the Lord manifests Himself simultaneously in many forms (prakasha), so that each devotee plays with Him in person.
  5. That is, Balarama and Jagannatha on the temple altar.
